scope: Close the two independent Reviewer P1 findings on ACT0: retain the identity-bound committed epoch audit after legitimate implementation/verification transitions, and restrict the ACT0-only feature-branch workflow to an explicit activation-audit trigger rather than every implementation push. No gameplay changes or gate weakening.
required_outputs: Preserved df1af401 machine PASS plus independent P1 findings
stop_conditions: Any required product or review predicate is waived
A historical event or policy must be rewritten
risk_reasons: Epoch audit governs runtime continuation beyond initial activation

design_brief.problem_statement: Independent Reviewer found that the recovery audit was gated on last work state DISPATCHED, and the ACT0-only feature job was triggered by all runtime pushes.
design_brief.current_behavior: The first legitimate IMPLEMENTATION_COMMITTED event loses the valid audit; ordinary gameplay changes fail a validator intended only for pre-implementation ACT0.
design_brief.desired_behavior: Audit validity follows exact epoch/main/provenance, not current product state. Ordinary runtime pushes do not run ACT0; explicit ACT0 audit runs retain all strict pre-implementation checks.
alternatives_considered: Accept arbitrary runtime diffs as ACT0
Ignore the independent P1 because all existing tests passed
design_brief.selected_design: Preserve the existing audit path and add MVP recovery audits in event order regardless of later state; keep exact committed identity and main checks. Gate feature-branch ACT0 execution on manual dispatch or an explicit [act0-audit] commit marker.
design_brief.why_selected: Corrects lifetime/scheduling ownership without altering gameplay, event reduction, or the definition of ACT0 success.
expected_risks: An old recovery audit masks a newer audit
A later main incorrectly reuses old proof
Ordinary feature pushes keep executing ACT0

notes: Reviewer comments 3967524197 and 3967524212 are binding blockers. df1af401 retained 296/296 machine PASS but is not accepted. This Work Order neither reuses nor invents an independent PASS. All changes use ordinary GitHub APIs; removed CI authoring is not reintroduced.
